_doc: N-TAGCOMP curve spec — the THIRD RR-EMIT spec and the second PRODUCTION
authoring run (nit was a lossless re-encoding; lag and this one author new
content). NOT loaded at runtime: app/domain/personas.py globs
content/personas/*.json non-recursively, so this subdirectory is invisible
to the pack loader. It is read only by backend/tools/rr_emit.py, which
emits the `unopened` nodes of the file named in `emits`.
PROVENANCE OF THE IDENTITY TARGET, stated ONCE here so the tests and the
pack can point at it instead of repeating a bare number: §5 TAG VPIP 15-20
/ PFR 12-17 (9-max full ring, online micro-low NL cash, ledger #14
full-ring-specialist source; confidence MEDIUM, band edges DIRECTIONAL).
Nothing in this slice gates on those edges — they are the reason the width
was HELD, not a target the content was fitted to. Measured population
readings quoted below come from metric #3
(tests/test_personas_postflop.py::_persona_stats_ext), whose lineup is 3x
the tested persona + 5 fillers, NOT the §5 reference pool: its readings are
one-sidedly biased and are comparable to EACH OTHER (before vs after), not
to a live tracker's population.
WHAT THIS REPAIRS (theory finding T-M2, wave-3 ledger; roadmap N-TAGCOMP):
the tag's opening composition was INVERTED against the shape the archetype
is named for. A TAG is the persona that plays nearly all of its suited
hands and is severely selective offsuit; the shipped ladder did the
opposite — at BTN it opened 69.9% of the suited universe against 51.3% of
the (three-times-larger) offsuit universe, i.e. 36.20% of ALL combos
offsuit against 16.44% suited. The surplus is dominated offsuit broadway
and offsuit kicker junk (K3o, Q4o, J6o from the button), which is exactly
the mass that plays worst multiway and worst out of position postflop.
THE FIX IS A COMPOSITION SWAP AT CONSTANT WIDTH, NOT A WIDEN OR A TRIM —
the N-LAGLADDER lesson, inherited deliberately. Offsuit falls and suited
rises at every one of the nine seats:
The combo-weighted TOTAL never RISES at any seat, and falls by at most
0.4525pp (HJ); seat-average 34.0204 -> 33.8529. Suited share of the suited
universe rises at every seat (BTN 69.9 -> 95.5, CO 57.1 -> 80.8, UTG 23.1
-> 34.0); offsuit share falls at every seat (BTN 51.3 -> 42.3, CO 41.7 ->
33.3, UTG 10.3 -> 6.4). Early seats cannot reach a high suited share at all
— the whole suited universe is 23.53% of combos, wider than the UTG range —
so the reachable statement there is the SUBSTITUTION, not the level.
WHY THE WIDTH IS NOT SPENT UPWARD — measured, not assumed. A 10-seed
metric-#3 sweep at n=2000 reads the pre-slice pack at VPIP 16.07 +- 0.53
and PFR 12.80 +- 0.46 — PFR sits 1.7 sd above the §5 floor of 12, i.e. with
no meaningful room to spend. Any real width increase pushes a persona that
is already wide per seat further from its dossier, and N-LAGLADDER's
abandoned first cut proved the symmetric hazard downward for the lag. So
the whole deliverable is the shape. Post-slice the same sweep reads VPIP
under one sd, which is what a constant-width swap should do and is
REPORTED, not gated (the single population band anchor is W4-b). Both stay
inside §5, as does the gap row (2-5): 3.27 -> 3.51.
⚠️ NOT CLAIMED: that these per-seat widths are RIGHT. They are the widths
this slice inherited, and at CO/BTN they sit well above a TAG dossier
envelope. Trimming toward it is filed work (N-TAGWIDTH) and needs the §5
PFR floor decision first; the width gate this slice ships is deliberately
ONE-SIDED so that trim is never blocked by a green test (see
tests/test_personas.py::test_tagcomp_total_width_never_rises).
PAIRS ARE UNTOUCHED at every seat (55+ UTG, 44+ UTG1/UTG2, 33+ LJ/BB, 22+
from HJ on), class-for-class and weight-for-weight. The swap is offsuit-for-
suited only; moving the pair band too would confound the measurement and is
not what T-M2 found.
AUTHORING RULE used for the offsuit rows (not enforced by the emitter, and
deliberately not gated — an authoring habit, not a law; carried over from
lag.unopened.json): a row never plays a weak kicker that a STRONGER high
card of the same kicker does not also play, so the weakest full-weight
kicker is non-decreasing down the rows (BTN: A2o, K5o, Q7o, J8o, T8o, 98o).
Suited rows are exempt: 65s outranks 95s on connectedness, so the
same-kicker comparison is not a domination relation there.
`depths[row]` = how many classes down that row the CORE tier plays, with
rows ordered strongest-kicker-first (As = AKs, AQs, ...). Rows absent from
`depths` are not played at all; a row present with depth 0 is played by the
slope tier only (the curve's leading edge spilling into a fresh row).
`slopes[row]` overrides the slope tier width for one row (one width per
slope tier); the tag uses `[0]` to stop a row cleanly at its core. A row
whose depth already covers the whole row needs no override — the emitter
clamps at the row end.
`raise_pct` is an ASSERTED ANNOTATION, never an emitter input: the combo-
weighted raise width the emitted node actually produces, cross-checked by
test_rr_emit.py. Floors are authored; they are never fitted to a target.
There is deliberately nowhere in this file to put a percentile or width
parameter (range-representation-design.md sec.1).
